header:
Date: 2026-05-03
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Solis (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Redwood Product), Priya Raman (Sapphire HoAI), Ethan Blake (Sapphire Platform), Laura Kim (Sapphire Finance), Samir Desai (Sapphire Security)
summary: Live console walkthrough focused on per-route telemetry, attribution and cost decomposition for Sapphire Health's multi-tenant inference workloads. Covered how Redwood maps tokens to routes, shows per-route SLOs, and configures fallback/rollout. Agreed to provide sandbox access and security docs; customer to upload routing config for benchmarking.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we have about 50 minutes, we'll run through the console sandbox and then leave time for Q&A. Priya: Thanks Maya, excited — we just want to see how cost ties back to our product routes.
[00:22] Derek Solis: Quick intro, I'm Derek, I'm the SE who will do the demo. Rina (product) is here for any product questions.
[00:35] Priya Raman: Our stack — currently on GCP, mix of T4 and some A10s for inference, we use an in-house router that tags requests with "route_id". We want per-route chargeback for billing and to stop noisy routes.
[00:50] Derek Solis: Perfect. Does your router attach expected latency SLOs and tenant tags today?
[00:58] Ethan Blake: We tag with tenant_id + route_id, we have an SLO for p95 < 300ms for interactive endpoints, but it's fuzzy.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Great. So the console will show token-level cost mapped to the route ID, and you can slice by tenant. We'll open the "Telemetry Sandbox" org now — note: link to deck / sandbox: https://redwood.ai/sandbox/sapphire-telemetry (shared).
[01:30] [02:05] Derek Solis: (screen share) Ok, top left is the org selector, then usage lens, you can see Requests per route, Token breakdown, and CPU/GPU time estimate. This chart is synthetic from the sandbox.
[02:35] Priya Raman: Is the GPU time estimate calibrated to A10 / T4? It looks low.
[02:45] Rina Patel: We surface model-profiled throughput data — you can pick the hardware profile. For customers we calibrate the estimate using model/seq-length histograms; sometimes the estimate will undercount if your tokenizer sets are different, so we recommend running a short benchmark.
[03:10] Samir Desai: Talk to me about security — where is the telemetry stored, do you leak PII in traces?
[03:20] Maya Chen: Good question. Telemetry is stored in the customer org in the Redwood control plane, logs can be configured to avoid payload capture. We integrate with KMS for envelope encryption and support customer-managed keys in Private. We'll send the SOC2 excerpt after this call.
[03:40] [04:05] Ethan Blake: Can we keep telemetry in our VPC? We prefer not to route raw requests out.
[04:12] Derek Solis: Yes, in Private deployments the control plane can sit in your VPC or on-prem; for hosted we do sanitized telemetry only. There are knobs — redaction, sampling rate, and payload suppression.
[04:35] Priya Raman: Show us the per-route cost breakdown.
[04:42] Derek Solis: Sure — switching to the Route Cost view. You see a waterfall: tokens, compute time, batching efficiency, caching effect. Each bar is clickable to drill into example requests (redacted).
[05:05] [05:40] Priya Raman: That caching line — is that the prefix/KV cache? We use context reuse heavily.
[05:48] Rina Patel: Yeah, prefix caching and KV cache are tracked as cache hits vs misses; hits lower effective token count. We also surface effective tokens after caching so your unit cost per logical token is accurate.
[06:10] Laura Kim: How do we attribute cost to product teams vs customers? We need monthly invoices per-team.
[06:20] Maya Chen: Two approaches: route-level mapping (you tag routes by product team) or tenant-level split. Console supports both and you can export per-route cost CSV for your internal billing. We also have an API endpoint for per-route aggregated metrics.
[06:42] Ethan Blake: Is the export incremental? We process a lot of data.
[06:48] Derek Solis: Yes exports are chunked and you can pull via S3 or direct API. For large volumes we recommend configuring daily aggregates.
[07:10] [07:45] Priya Raman: Tell us about rollouts and automatic fallback. We have bursty traffic and we need graceful degradation to cheaper models.
[07:55] Rina Patel: Rollouts in the Console let you specify a policy: by latency or cost fallback. For example, if p95 for route exceeds threshold, redirect a % of traffic to a cheaper model variant, or route to Dedicated capacity. You can preview the routing decision tree in the UI.
[08:20] Ethan Blake: Do we get real-time tracing to see which requests hit fallback?
[08:26] Derek Solis: Yes, traces include the decision path but not full prompt text unless you enable payload capture; trace IDs map back to per-route entries.
[08:45] [09:10] Maya Chen: I'll do a quick walkthrough of setting an alert — Alerts > New > route p95 > 300ms > notify Slack. You can also add runbook links and on-call rotations.
[09:35] Priya Raman: Ok that's helpful. On the cost modeling side, what's the typical error margin on compute estimates?
[09:45] Rina Patel: For model types we support the profiling error is about +/- 8-12% depending on tokenization and batch distribution. If you run a 1k request benchmark with your routing config we'll calibrate it to under 5%.
[10:10] [10:40] Laura Kim: For procurement, we need committed spend predictability. Do you do reserved capacity and can we see committed vs on-demand consumption in the Console?
[10:50] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated (reserved) pools show committed utilization dashboards. You can set alerts when on-demand usage exceeds X% of reserved. We'll show that in the sandbox — switching to "Dedicated Pools" tab.
[11:20] Derek Solis: Also, cost breakdown per-route will attribute the fraction backed by reserved v. on-demand.
[11:45] [12:10] Samir Desai: For audits, how granular are your audit logs? We need request-level metadata for 90 days.
[12:20] Maya Chen: Audit logs include request metadata (timestamps, route_id, model variant, decision path) and admin actions. For Private installs you can configure retention and send logs to your SIEM. We'll include an excerpt in the security pack.
[12:45] [13:05] Derek Solis: Now the "Hot Routes" view — this shows top N routes by token spend and their trend lines. You can click a route and get top 20 example requests (redacted) and a cost-explainer that shows why it's expensive (long seqs, low cache hit, small batching).
[13:35] Priya Raman: Can we run a what-if: increase batch size by 2x and see projected cost savings?
[13:45] Rina Patel: Yes, there's a cost simulator — adjust batch, enable quantization, enable prefix caching, and it will recompute estimated cost per 1M tokens. It uses model-specific kernels profile.
[14:10] [14:35] Ethan Blake: Quantization — our models include some finetuned variants, are they supported?
[14:42] Derek Solis: We support many quant profiles; for finetuned checkpoints we recommend running the small calibration job in sandbox. The console will suggest quant profiles with expected accuracy delta.
[15:00] [15:28] Maya Chen: A live example: route "patient-note-extract" — high tokens because clients send full note. I click in, shows avg seq 1,240 tokens, cache hit 4%, cost per request 0.015 USD.
[15:45] Priya Raman: Ouch, that's our problem. Can we do prefix stripping at the edge?
[15:52] Derek Solis: Yes you can configure pre-processing hooks or use built-in prompt templates to strip irrelevant sections, and cache more aggressively.
[16:10] [16:40] Laura Kim: If we change prompts and reduce tokens by 30% does the console show historical retroactive savings?
[16:48] Rina Patel: We have a retroactive scenario simulator: apply hypothetical token reduction and it replays cost over a window to show estimated savings. It's approximate.
[17:10] [17:42] Priya Raman: For the benchmarking you mentioned, what artifacts do you need?
[17:48] Derek Solis: A routing config, sample request traces (anonymized), and model mapping per route. We'll run a 1k synthetic run in sandbox.
[18:05] Samir Desai: Is there an SLA for Dedicated? We need 99.9 for certain clinical features.
[18:14] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; details in the enterprise contract. We'll attach the SLA doc.
[18:35] [19:05] Priya Raman: About pricing model — per-token for hosted, committed for Dedicated, is there a hybrid?
[19:12] Rina Patel: You can combine: reserved pools for core traffic and hosted for bursts. Console will estimate blended unit cost and show you cost-optimal routing.
[19:35] Ethan Blake: Can the router do weighted policies by time-of-day? We have nightly batch jobs.
[19:42] Derek Solis: Yes, routing policies can include schedule rules.
[20:05] [20:40] Derek Solis: Jumping back to Alerts, you can create anomaly detection on per-route spend spikes which triggers a Slack webhook and optionally an automated throttling action.
[21:02] Priya Raman: What's the false positive rate on anomaly detection?
[21:10] Rina Patel: Depends on tuning; default sensitivity is conservative — we commonly tune the window and min-request thresholds. For big bursts it's reliable.
[21:35] [22:05] Maya Chen: I'll show the per-tenant billing export — CSV fields: date, route_id, tenant_id, tokens, compute_seconds, cost_usd, reserved_fraction. You can set export cadence.
[22:25] Ethan Blake: Nice. For finance we need mapping to our internal charge codes. Can we attach a mapping table?
[22:32] Derek Solis: Yes, export supports enrichment via mapping files or a mapping UI where you map route_id to charge code.
[22:55] [23:20] Priya Raman: Ok demo looks strong. A few follow-ups from security: payload redaction options and KMS integration.
[23:30] Samir Desai: We also want to see the network topology for Private — where the control plane sits.
[23:38] Maya Chen: We'll include network diagrams and KMS docs in the packet. Also we have a checklist for FedRAMP direction if needed.
[23:55] [24:20] Derek Solis: Quick note: metrics latency — Console shows near-real-time metrics with ~15s ingest latency for hosted, and can be configured for lower latency in Dedicated with heavier infra.
[24:42] Priya Raman: Good. One more question: how do you handle model regressions? We need quality monitoring tied to prompt sets.
[24:52] Rina Patel: Redwood Optimize can run evals on golden prompts and alert if output quality drifts. We can tie regressions to rollbacks. We'll show an example in a subsequent session.
[25:20] [25:50] Laura Kim: From procurement perspective, can we get a short T&Cs summary? We need to know data residency and indemnity.
[25:58] Maya Chen: We'll include the procurement starter pack.
[26:15] [26:45] Priya Raman: Ok let's talk timeline: we'd like to run a pilot in the next 2-3 weeks.
[26:52] Maya Chen: Great. We'll provision a 3-day sandbox and run the benchmark Monday once you upload traces.
[27:05] Derek Solis: I'll also annotate any costly routes and propose quick wins (prompt fixes, caching).
[27:22] [27:50] Priya Raman: Can we invite someone from infra to the sandbox? Ethan will coordinate.
[27:56] Ethan Blake: Yep, I'll get the routing config by Friday.
[28:10] [28:40] Maya Chen: Recap — action items: send SOC2 excerpt, provision sandbox, customer to upload traces and routing config, run benchmark, follow-up for Optimize session.
[29:05] Rina Patel: Any other questions?
[29:12] Priya Raman: Not right now — thanks.
[29:20] Derek Solis: One last note: we have sample quantization tradeoff reports, I'll attach a sample.
[29:30] [END OF MAIN DEMO]

[30:00] Off-record chatter and screen fiddling for ~10 minutes, brief pause.

[40:05] [Q&A continuing]
[40:12] Laura Kim: If we sign a Dedicated contract, is there a migration path?
[40:20] Maya Chen: Yes we do in-place migration with traffic split and can orchestrate cutover.
[40:35] Samir Desai: For compliance audits, can logs be immutable and stored in our S3?
[40:44] Derek Solis: Yes, we support S3 archiving with object lock for immutability.
[40:58] Priya Raman: Are there any common pitfalls you see on onboarding?
[41:06] Rina Patel: Common pitfalls: untagged routes, missing tokenization alignment, and not calibrating batch sizes. We provide a checklist and a short onboarding sprints.
[41:28] [42:00] Maya Chen: Alright we'll leave the recordings and artifacts uploaded to the sandbox org. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security pack and sandbox invite.
[42:23] Ethan Blake: Thanks all.
[42:30] Priya Raman: Thanks, bye.

[END]
